title: Sadly, my UE5 Plugin failed commercially I and cannot longer support it, so I just made it 100% free on FAB
author: MHVANMX
selftext:
**Asset Context Exporter For AI** is a plugin I made as an alternative to expensive AI Agents/Copilots, by basically turning your UE5 assets into text files easy to drag and drop into any LLM chatbox, saving you all the trouble of explaining each asset in your project and therefore giving it that full context an embedded copilot has.

It's been approximately 6 months since I've first released this tool under the name "Context Bridge For Unreal" on Gumroad, and 3 months since I've uploaded to FAB under its current name, despite overhauling the tool, adding functions and improving the file outputs, unfortunately, it only had a single sale throughout said months, I can't stand it anymore and simply want to move on :(  


The link will take you to my plugin's FAB page if you are interested, I hope it becomes useful and an essential part of your workflow, good luck with your games, and remember, don't let AI take over your work, use it to improve it : )

comments.author: adpowah
comments.body: Making it free and then including it as part of your portfolio is a great option if it wasn’t commercially viable.

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: It might be, but as of today I will be focusing entirely on my own game

replies.author: Lordxb
replies.body: Best make tools commercially viable by doing massive research on the market before dedicating your time to a project!! Lesson learned and making game is another rabbit hole that tends to equal same results so do the research first not just make it and end up with few sales!!

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: You are right, I first started it as a personal tool, my first ever version ran using .bat commands, it just kept growing until I decided to turn it into a public plugin, seeing all those simple questions people often have on these forums made me think I could have relative success, looks like people will rather wait for random people to answer their questions than to use AI to pinpoint their issue...

replies.author: Lordxb
replies.body: Your direction was always good but market just was not interested in paying for it unfortunately!!

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: I appreciate it : ) And, yeah, I learned the hard way, but we just have to move on and not get stuck

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: Thanks to you for giving it a try, hope it's useful : )

comments.author: InsensitiveClown
comments.body: You did well in open-sourcing it. Ensure it is part of your CV and that licensing, authorship, contact information and linkedin profile is accessible. It wasn't successful as a commercial product, but it may be successful showing your skills. So, stay positive, and kudos for opening it.

comments.author: Legitimate-Salad-101
comments.body:
The name alone is sort of hard to understand what it does. It’s not something that’s going to be searched for. 

Did you market it at all?

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body:
The tool itself is hard to explain other than simply saying "It converts your assets into AI readable files", but from I could research, that description was already being used by plenty of other tools that do only a quarter of what mine does, so that's the best name I could come up with, trying my best not to get related to those simple dumpers.

Other than showing it across some communities, not really, I would only about 11k people saw it, FAB doesn't provide Analytics so it's just a guess. Even then, I never realized how Anti AI the UE community can be, despite my efforts on not to be related to the previously mentioned tools, people will just read "LLM" or "AI" and will instantly call it 'slop' or assume my plugin would just do an unoptimized text dump

replies.author: Legitimate-Salad-101
replies.body:
Ya, people call everything Slop instantly. I’m not sure how many devs are using AI with UE, it could only be 11k for all I know. 

But most people don’t even finish a plugin, let alone post it on FAB. That alone was a big one. Congrats!

comments.author: Rust_Mayhem_Artifice
comments.body: This sounds awesome, will be giving it a go. Thanks for making it available and sharing!

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: Thanks to you for giving it a try, hope it's useful : )

replies.author: Rust_Mayhem_Artifice
replies.body: This seems very useful, thank you! I will play with the settings more, I'm messing around with creating a game manually using blueprints but prompting ChatGPT, so I'm new to all of this. I tried exporting only blueprints in a Monolithic file to Chat but it is too big. If I enable file splitting it creates a blueprint folder but then I think I'd need to import only relevant blueprints. Is there a way to have it act Monlithic but split the master file into smaller pieces? I assumed that's what the file splitting would do.

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: File splitting works the same as a normal non monolithic export, the 'split' refers to each individual file being cut into multiple files if it's weight surpasses the set "MAX FILE SIZE", for example, if one of your exported blueprints weights 2MB, enabling the file splitting with a max file size of 5MB will result in your blueprint being separated into 5 1MB files, currently the splitting doesn't apply to monolithic exports, I've never truly considered splitting the monolithic files given that just a single 1MB file is already too much for most LLMs. How much does your Blueprint monolithic file weight?

replies.author: Rust_Mayhem_Artifice
replies.body: The BP monolithic file is 6.2MB. I realize it's probably not a good idea to dump the entire BP list into a LLM and rather to select specific BPs, but I wanted to give it a shot! When I tried importing the Master JSON it failed to see it, but when converting to a text file it at least captured part of the content. Either way this is very helpful, I can easily paste a BP JSON instead of a bunch of manual screenshots. Thank you!

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body:
Those are some chubby BP haha, right away 6.2MB may not sound like a lot, but given it's just plain text, it translates to millions worth of tokens and words, when I was doing tests myself, Chat GPT was the most inefficient reading the exported files, giving it any export beyond 500Kb felt incredibly inconsistent, sometimes it read it perfectly, but most of the times it felt as if it just read a bunch of chunks at random.

That's actually my preferred way to use it, unless you are paying 200$ for the most premium plan of any LLM, trying to feed it your full project all at once will be almost the same as not giving it anything at all.
Yeah! It's a 1000x better, best thing is it's not just your graph, the designer and components inside your BPs/WPSs are exported as well, and, you're welcome : )

replies.author: Rust_Mayhem_Artifice
replies.body: I’ve been using this the last couple days and it’s been so much nicer than pasting screenshots. Thanks again!

replies.author: MHVANMX
replies.body: Hello again! You must have noticed already, given some $$$ trouble I had recently, I decided to give my plugin one last chance, I hope you are enjoying version 1.1 : D
